stories.title: The canvas has stopped waiting for instructions
stories.blurb: Aurélie Radom uses Miro's agentic canvas as the worked example: context from Slack, GitHub, Amplitude and Granola lands in one space, Sidekicks read it and produce documents, diagrams or prototypes, and Flows turn those into reusable workflows. Her argument is that Nielsen's heuristics do not expire here, they change meaning. Visibility of system status now means a person has to be able to see what the agent understood and what it already changed.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: When the canvas starts acting, who’s really in control?

stories.title: An illustrator draws first, then the agent inherits the rules
stories.blurb: Tom May had criticised The Working Assembly's identity for the journaling app Untold and got an account of the method back. Founder Jolene Delisle describes a commissioned human illustration made first, a custom agent built around it under a fixed set of creative rules, and outputs reworked for texture, tone, lighting and composition. The justification is functional rather than financial: the illustration has to respond to what someone is expressing, which a fixed library cannot do.

stories.title: A university puts its own place name back into the wordmark
stories.blurb: rbl has rebuilt the University of East Anglia around the organising idea 'Original by nature', after consulting over 100 stakeholders and gathering input from more than 800 members of the university. Three things carry it: the location now sits in the wordmark, the long-standing glint symbol has become a curved beacon, and the palette is drawn from Norfolk. Strategy director Rhiannon Lowe says the story was already there and simply was not being told.

stories.title: A book bans the moodboard and proposes three phases instead
stories.blurb: Erik Herrström, formerly leading brand design at Spotify, sets out a method against the reference loop in The Echo: Immerse, Create, Impact. The first phase permits no moodboards and no early visual references, requiring ethnographic and subcultural research before any design software is opened. Reviewer Pushkar Mankar rates it a thoughtful piece of work but doubts it undoes the economic pressures pushing studios toward safe, automated choices.

stories.title: Perplexity needed several passes to produce a usable tetrad
stories.blurb: Theresa-Marie Rhyne continues testing how well language models build colour harmonies for data visualisation, adding Perplexity after DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and Gemini. The model fixated on colour deficiency first and returned no proper tetrad at all; only revised prompts produced an approximate one. Take the suggestion, then check it against the rule, not only against a contrast test.

stories.title: The US government calls training on other people's text fair use
stories.blurb: The Justice Department filed an amicus brief in the New York Times case against OpenAI, siding with the AI companies. Its argument separates the copying done for training from the model's public outputs, which it says are often not substantially similar to the originals. The filing runs against the Copyright Office report that had rejected a blanket fair use for AI training.

stories.title: ByteDance buys its way into the creative awards
stories.blurb: CapCut becomes the One Club's global AI partner, and the list is specific: presenting partner of ADC Young Guns 24 and of the One Show 2027 Creative Use of AI discipline, its own brief in the Young Ones Student Awards, plus a new custom AI category for the ADC Annual Awards to be announced in October 2026. Judgment on generative work will now happen inside a frame paid for by a maker of generative tools.

stories.title: Gemini now picks which parts of a video it bothers to watch
stories.blurb: Instead of sampling a video evenly frame by frame, the model decides for itself which segment to look at, at what frame rate and through which modality, image, audio or transcript. Google reports up to 88 percent fewer tokens on LVBench and 1H-VideoQA, roughly 66 percent lower cost per request, and slightly better accuracy. Available for Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite.

sources.name: Google DeepMind
sources.headline: Introducing agentic video understanding with Gemini

stories.title: The third Flash model in six weeks thinks longer and eats more
stories.blurb: Gemini 3.8 Flash ships in a general and a cyber-specialised variant and reaches 73.7 percent on DeepSWE v1.1 for long-horizon software engineering. Introductory pricing matches the three-week-old predecessor at $0.75 and $3.75 per million tokens, then doubles after January 2027. The catch sits in the mechanism: the extra reasoning steps consume around 40 percent more tokens, which eats part of the price advantage back.
